categories.name: Agent Security Research
categories.summary: A dominant theme today centers on treating AI agents as untrusted system components requiring external controls rather than relying on model robustness alone. Multiple papers explore the attack surface created by agent 'skills' and third-party integrations, with researchers mapping real attacks to classic systems-security failures like missing least privilege and instruction/data separation.

key_items.title: Agent security requires systems thinking, not model hardening
key_items.detail: CSO coverage of research mapping 11 real agent attacks to systems-security failures argues models should be treated as untrusted with controls enforced around them.

key_items.title: Agentic coding assistants as attacker shells
key_items.detail: Research demonstrates how unvetted external artifacts with hidden prompt-injection can steer coding agents to execute file edits or commands, emphasizing tool/action policy enforcement.

key_items.title: Agent Skills architecture and security path forward
key_items.detail: Paper examines how on-demand skill loading via MCP shifts trust boundaries to the skill acquisition layer, questioning how progressive disclosure can constrain untrusted skills.

categories.name: AI Supply Chain Security
categories.summary: Research efforts focus on scanning and validating agent 'skills' before they enter production environments. Tools like SkillSpector and SkillsMetric address the emerging threat of malicious skill packages through static analysis, while acknowledging limitations that necessitate runtime controls for certain attack patterns.

key_items.title: SkillSpector scans agent skills pre-deployment
key_items.detail: Scanner examines skills as code plus model-visible instructions, detecting prompt injection, metadata poisoning, permission mismatches, and vulnerable dependencies with SARIF-ready output.

key_items.title: SkillsMetric maps static analysis detection limits
key_items.detail: Framework scores skill packages with static signals and measures where detection breaks on adversarial datasets, identifying which behaviors require runtime rather than scan-time controls.

categories.name: Prompt Injection & SSRF Vulnerabilities
categories.summary: Concrete vulnerability disclosures and research highlight how prompt injection chains can drive agents toward dangerous actions. A notable advisory demonstrates SSRF attacks against MCP servers that can expose IAM credentials through cloud metadata endpoints, with specific defensive mitigations provided.

key_items.title: MCP SSRF advisory for Anthropic and Microsoft tools
key_items.detail: Full Disclosure advisory describes prompt-injection driven SSRF chains reaching cloud metadata endpoints. Defenses include URL allowlists, RFC1918 blocking, redirect validation, and IMDSv2.

key_items.title: LLM reviewers vulnerable to invisible-font injection
key_items.detail: Benchmark across 12 LLMs shows hidden instructions in papers can steer review scores to acceptance-level, necessitating input sanitization for automated review workflows.

categories.name: AI Governance & Trust Frameworks
categories.summary: New research proposes architectural approaches to agent governance through verifiable provenance and hierarchical policy composition. The KYA framework introduces an 'only-tighten' rule for policy inheritance and signed recommendation verification to prevent silent behavioral drift.

key_items.title: KYA trust layer for autonomous systems
key_items.detail: Framework-agnostic trust layer verifies signed recommendations at ingest and composes hierarchical policies with only-tighten rules, adding principal scoring and audit-friendly delegation attribution.

categories.name: Security Evaluation Frameworks
categories.summary: ClawDojo emerges as a benchmark harness for systematically testing prompt-injection and supply-chain attacks against defensive measures, focusing on architectural attack surfaces like persistent memory and third-party skill integrations in OpenClaw-style agents.

key_items.title: ClawDojo evaluation framework for agent attacks and defenses
key_items.detail: Dynamic benchmark harness tests prompt-injection and supply-chain skill abuse against candidate defenses, framing security around architectural attack surface analysis.

categories.name: Standards & Reference Materials
categories.summary: OWASP continues expanding its agentic AI security guidance with crosswalk documentation mapping the Top 10 for Agentic Applications to related frameworks, providing practitioners with actionable reference materials for securing agent deployments.

key_items.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications crosswalks
key_items.detail: Reference resource mapping OWASP's agentic application risks to other security frameworks for compliance and implementation alignment.

categories.name: Threat Intelligence
categories.summary: Research into background C2 agent techniques surfaces, indicating ongoing investigation into how AI agents could be weaponized for command-and-control operations, representing an evolution in threat actor tradecraft.

key_items.title: Background C2 agent research
key_items.detail: Origin HQ publishes research on background command-and-control agent techniques, exploring adversarial use of AI agent capabilities.

top_insights: The security community is converging on a 'zero trust model' paradigm—treating LLMs as fundamentally untrusted components requiring external enforcement rather than internal robustness improvements.
Agent 'skills' and MCP integrations represent the new software supply chain threat vector, with multiple papers releasing detection tools and acknowledging static analysis limitations.
SSRF via prompt injection is now a documented attack pattern against production MCP servers, with concrete IAM credential exposure risks in cloud environments.
Invisible/hidden text prompt injection remains effective against state-of-the-art models in automated workflows, from peer review to coding assistants.
Hierarchical policy composition with 'only-tighten' semantics is emerging as an architectural pattern for preventing silent privilege escalation in multi-agent systems.
